title: Make 'Show in Explorer' land on the right item at paths over 260 characters, and on folders the user cannot open
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: 1. Revealing a folder the user cannot open (deny-all ACE) opens its readable parent with that folder selected, with no error dialog and no elevation prompt. Verified by a test that reads the Explorer window's folder and selection through Shell.Application and compares the leaf Name.: partial

2. At paths of about 161, 300 and 1000 characters, the right leaf is selected in the right parent within 1 s. Compared by leaf Name or GetLongPathName-resolved paths, never Explorer's literal (8.3) path strings (U-114).: partial

3. The reveal goes only through SHParseDisplayName and SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems. Nothing in the app starts explorer.exe /select, not even as a fallback. Enforced by review plus an architecture rule that catches any launch of explorer.exe with /select.: partial
4. A landing counts as good only when the window's folder and selection say so; an exit code or HRESULT alone is never taken as success (asserted by the tests in criteria 1 and 2).: partial

5. The shipped 'Open in Explorer' on tree and biggest-files items (SC-007) goes through this same reveal; its existing window cases still pass; plus a new case at a path of 300 or more characters.: partial

6. A reveal that cannot land (e.g. the target's parent was deleted) tells the person so, and no other folder is opened in its place. Tested by deleting the parent, then asserting no Explorer window opens and the app shows a failure message.: missing

Criterion 4 says an exit code or HRESULT alone is never success, and names the window tests as its check. This design reads it as binding the tests only: the app still reports Exact, and shows its success text, from hr==0. The spike shows this gives a false success for Hidden+System items (0 of 8 selected under your settings). Is that acceptable for SL-088, with H+S going to a follow-on slice, or should the app itself confirm the landing through Explorer's windows before saying it succeeded? The second answer adds COM automation of Explorer to the shipped exe and changes the reveal contract.

The select-switch rule counts comments (SL-087's `including_comments: true` form), so any explanatory comment in ShellReveal.cs must avoid spelling the switch. A reviewer may prefer comments to be excluded.
R-002 as a new case versus growing R-001 with the SL-088 steps.
Adding a `Failed` kind versus reusing an existing failure member of RevealKind, and the naming of the refusal reason.
Status wording ('Rescan to refresh', 'Nothing was opened'), and keeping a refusal on the status line rather than in a dialog.
Hidden+System targets (case C-014, not material) remain out of this slice, as the design decided.

The product still does not confirm a landing through Explorer's windows (criterion 4 as designed; the open question stands). The new resolve-back check confirms only that the shell's parse stands for the item.

A person, or validate with permission to open and close Explorer windows, runs `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case R-002` and `-Case R-001`. That settles criteria 1, 2 and 5 and the cold 1000 ms bound.

Measure once whether Shell.Application's Quit() on one tab's entry closes only that tab (Windows 11 tabbed Explorer). If it does, Close-CaseWindows could also close a case tab that sits beside the person's tabs, instead of reporting it.
Windows 10 was not measured. There, a device name with an extension is expected to be refused by the parse's HRESULT or by the resolve-back check rather than landing. A run there would say which.
A follow-on slice for Hidden+System reveals once that spike has run at Windows' default Explorer settings.

caused_by.reason: validation partial this build: Rebuild SL-088. The validation was right. O-015 is a real product defect, confirmed against the real shell on Windows 11 26200. ShellReveal.Plan (ShellReveal.cs:138-140) takes the reserved-name base from the text before the first dot. So it refuses con.txt, aux.h, nul.log, com1.txt and prn.md as NameUnaddressable, even though SHParseDisplayName returns S_OK and resolves each one to the exact file. The app would falsely say Explorer can't select them and open nothing. Fix: refuse up front only the names the shell really can't address (bare reserved names like 'co…
